evals.expected_output: A structured vulnerability report covering: SQL injection in getUsers (fmt.Sprintf into SQL query), OS command injection in runCommand (exec.Command with sh -c), SSRF in fetchURL (user-controlled URL), error message information leakage (raw err.Error() returned to client), and no authentication/authorization on any routes. Report must include vulnerable code snippets, call chains, PoCs with HTTP requests, root causes, and remediations.
assertions: The report identifies the SQL injection vulnerability in the getUsers handler
The report identifies the OS command injection vulnerability in the runCommand handler
The report identifies the SSRF vulnerability in the fetchURL handler
The report includes at least one PoC HTTP request per injection finding
Each finding includes a call chain tracing from the HTTP route to the vulnerable line
Each finding includes a root cause explanation
Each finding includes a remediation with a Go code example
The report includes an executive summary with total findings by severity
The report identifies the missing authentication/authorization on routes

evals.expected_output: A structured vulnerability report covering: weak JWT secret (hardcoded 'secret'), JWT algorithm confusion (ParseToken does not verify signing method), MD5 used for password hashing (weak, no salt), path traversal in DownloadFile (filepath.Join does not prevent traversal to parent directories), math/rand used for security-sensitive reset token generation (not cryptographically secure), raw error returned to client in DownloadFile. Each finding must have severity, code snippet, call chain, root cause, PoC, and remediation.
assertions: The report identifies the hardcoded JWT secret and rates it High or Critical
The report identifies the JWT algorithm confusion vulnerability in ParseToken
The report identifies MD5 as a weak password hashing algorithm
The report identifies the path traversal vulnerability in DownloadFile
The report identifies math/rand as cryptographically insecure for token generation
The path traversal finding includes a PoC showing how to read /etc/passwd or similar
The JWT finding includes a remediation showing how to verify the signing method
The MD5 finding recommends bcrypt or argon2 as a replacement
The report has an executive summary

evals.expected_output: A structured vulnerability report covering: Zip Slip path traversal in extractZip (zip entries with ../ in names written to arbitrary paths), server-side template injection in templateHandler (user-controlled template string), unbounded JSON body read in uploadHandler (DoS via large payload, missing http.MaxBytesReader), concurrent unsynchronized map write in processPayload (data race on cache map), unbounded goroutine spawning in uploadHandler (goroutine leak/DoS). Report must have full structure including PoCs.
assertions: The report identifies the Zip Slip vulnerability in the extractZip handler
The report identifies server-side template injection in the templateHandler
The report identifies the missing request body size limit (http.MaxBytesReader)
The report identifies the concurrent unsynchronized map write as a data race
The Zip Slip finding includes a PoC showing a crafted zip entry with ../ in the filename
The template injection finding includes a PoC showing a malicious template string
The data race finding explains why writing to a Go map concurrently is unsafe
The report has a finding summary table with all issues
Remediations include correct Go code patterns (filepath.Clean check, html/template safety note, http.MaxBytesReader, sync.RWMutex)
